recognize_zh: 周邊血液中可見一顆核卵圓、染色質細緻、細胞質少而淡藍的母細胞（blast），緊鄰一顆佈滿粗大深紫色顆粒的嗜鹼性球；循環母細胞合併嗜鹼性球為t(6;9) AML常見的組合線索。
features: Single circulating blast with oval nucleus, fine chromatin, high N:C ratio and a thin rim of pale basophilic agranular cytoplasm
Adjacent basophil with abundant coarse dark purple granules obscuring the nucleus
No Auer rod discernible in the blast in this field
Background red cells normocytic and normochromic with few poikilocytes; platelets not prominent
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a circulating blast with an oval nucleus, finely dispersed chromatin and scant pale blue agranular cytoplasm, lying next to a basophil packed with coarse purple-black granules. Red cells are largely normocytic and normochromic. An Auer rod is not evident in this blast. In context, findings are suggestive of acute myeloid leukemia with basophilia, as seen in AML with t(6;9)(p23;q34); DEK::NUP214; bone marrow evaluation with cytogenetics is required.

ddx.vs: Features basophilia with a left-shifted granulocytic series and leukocytosis, and is defined by BCR::ABL1 on FISH/PCR.

ddx.dx: Reactive lymphocyte or large granular lymphocyte
ddx.vs: Reactive lymphocytes have more condensed chromatin and abundant cytoplasm, lacking the fine blastic chromatin and high N:C ratio.
Lymphoblasts can look similar on morphology, so flow cytometry (MPO, CD13/CD33/CD117 versus CD19/CD10 or cCD3) is needed; accompanying basophilia favors a myeloid process.
